title: Listing community widgets in the documentation
body:
cc @Shipow @speedblue, I saw some documentation website screenshots where we have community widget documentation along with our widgets (using Author: @algolia etc..)

I feel for a start and even in the future as for community widgets we could have a dedicated page accessible on the left navigation that will list the community widgets and their github.

Trying to have community widgets mixed with official ones on the same page will be confusing: you'll have to maintain the documentation for things we do not maintain.

This would be like jquery website having community widget documentation on the main website: seems confusing for a developer I think.

A simple page that we will create once we have community widgets should be enough for a start.

WDYT?

comments.body:
So I would propose:
- every good community widget ends up in the community widget list (link to github + demo if available)
- for instantsearch.js launch, we (algolia) build some widgets in github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js-$widget. Like instantseach.js-googleMap
- we list this as a community widget: this is not something in the core and so should not be listed in the main documentation but rather have his own small documentation + demo on gh pages in his github

As a user it's really important to be able to distinguish the core widgets from the community widgets. jQuery ui for instance do not have the documentation/demos for community widgets on the main website. Which is good, for clarity and maintenance.

Then if at some point we want to have a dedicated website/page demoing all the community widgets (sort of widgets portal), then maybe we will be able to do so. But I find this overkill most of the time.
Sorry this was answered/discussed in slack/asana.
